title: Identical probes: Law 5 for the records, single-instance and pair distances

key_results.statement: For $C=C^{(1)}+C^{(2)}$ with records $K^{(1)}_h$, $K^{(2)}_h$ and $\Delta_h:=K^{(1)}_h-K^{(2)}_h$, the swap defect is $D:=P_{12}CP_{12}-C=\sum_{a,b}\lvert ab\rangle\langle ab\rvert\otimes(\Delta_b-\Delta_a)$, i.e. $D(\lvert ab\rangle\otimes\xi)=\lvert ab\rangle\otimes(\Delta_b-\Delta_a)\xi$.

For two probes of one type ($d_T\ge2$) recorded by one medium, either family, with $\mathcal H_{\rm adm}=\{\Psi:P_{12}\Psi=c_T\Psi\}$: $e^{-iC\lambda}\mathcal H_{\rm adm}\subseteq\mathcal H_{\rm adm}$ for all $\lambda$ $\iff(P_{12}CP_{12}-C)\mathcal H_{\rm adm}=0\iff\Delta_h$ is independent of $h$.
For the same contract system, $P_{12}CP_{12}=C$ iff $\Delta_h$ is independent of $h$; this is not the condition $\Delta=0$.
The termwise property $P_{12}C^{(1)}P_{12}=C^{(2)}$ holds iff $K^{(1)}_h=K^{(2)}_h$ for all $h$, i.e. iff $\Delta=0$; it depends on how $C$ is split into its two contract terms.

The splits of a given $C$ into two contract terms differ exactly by $K^{(1)}_h\to K^{(1)}_h+X$, $K^{(2)}_h\to K^{(2)}_h-X$ with $X=X^\dagger$ on $\mathcal H_c$ independent of $h$, so $\Delta_h\to\Delta_h+2X$ (the A5 freedom to assign the medium-only term to either contract); hence $C$ is swap-invariant iff it has a split with $\Delta=0$, and the value of $\Delta$ is a convention of the description (M6) while only its $h$-dependence is a property of $C$.

For $h$-independent $\Delta$ and $K_h:=K^{(1)}_h$: $C=\sum_h\bigl(\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert_{p_1}+\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert_{p_2}\bigr)\otimes K_h-\mathbb 1_{p_1p_2}\otimes\Delta$, i.e. the swap-invariant contract system with $K^{(1)}_h=K^{(2)}_h=K_h$ minus a medium-only term.

For $C=\sum_h\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert\otimes M_h$ with $M_h=M_h^\dagger$ and a product start $\lvert\Phi\rangle\otimes\lvert\omega\rangle$ of unit vectors with $\Phi_h\neq0$: $\lvert\psi_h(\lambda)\rangle=\Phi_h\,e^{-iM_h\lambda}\lvert\omega\rangle$, hence $p_h=\lvert\Phi_h\rvert^2>0$ and $W(h,h';\lambda)=\lvert\langle\omega\vert e^{iM_{h'}\lambda}e^{-iM_h\lambda}\vert\omega\rangle\rvert^2$ exactly.

In the setting of (12.8), with $W(h,h';\lambda)=1-\lambda^2\lVert Q_\omega(M_h-M_{h'})\omega\rVert^2+O(\lambda^3)$ and $Q_\omega=\mathbb 1_{\bar A}-\lvert\omega\rangle\langle\omega\rvert$: $\lim_{\lambda\to0^+}\alpha(h,h';\lambda)/\lambda=\lVert Q_\omega(M_h-M_{h'})\omega\rVert$.

For $M_h=B_h+C_{\bar A}$ with $C_{\bar A}$ independent of $h$ ($C_A=0$, $C_\partial=\sum_h\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert\otimes B_h$): $\lim_{\lambda\to0^+}\alpha(h,h';\lambda)/\lambda=\lVert\tilde u_h-\tilde u_{h'}\rVert$ with $\lvert\tilde u_h\rangle=Q_\omega B_h\lvert\omega\rangle$, which is (11.6) and (11.8) with $(\phi,\chi)\to(\Phi,\omega)$; the types of the objects enter nowhere.

For $c_T=+1$, $\Delta$ independent of $h$ and the start $\lvert\phi\rangle\otimes\lvert\phi\rangle\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$ with $\phi_h\neq0$, the cut $\{p_1\}\mid\{p_2,c\}$ has $d_0(h,h')=\lim_{\lambda\to0^+}\alpha(h,h';\lambda)/\lambda=\lVert u_h-u_{h'}\rVert$, $\lvert u_h\rangle=(K_h-\langle K_h\rangle)\lvert\chi\rangle$: the value (5.10) of a single probe recorded alone, the same for $p_2$, independent of $\phi$, $\Delta$ and the split.

In the same setting, for the cut $\{p_1,p_2\}\mid\{c\}$ the leading-order distance between joint places is $d_0\bigl((h_1,h_2),(h_1',h_2')\bigr)=\lVert u_{h_1}+u_{h_2}-u_{h_1'}-u_{h_2'}\rVert$, independent of $\Delta$.
In the same setting, $W\bigl((h_1,h_2),(h_2,h_1);\lambda\bigr)=1$ for every $\lambda$: swapped joint places are one point of $X_V$, exactly.

For joint places that differ in one probe place only, $d_0\bigl((h_1,h_2),(h_1',h_2)\bigr)=\lVert u_{h_1}-u_{h_1'}\rVert=d_0(h_1,h_1')$ for every spectator place $h_2$: the pair distance equals the single-instance value (12.12).

For $c_T=+1$, $h\neq h'$ and the admissible start $\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(\lvert hh'\rangle+\lvert h'h\rangle\bigr)\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$: in the single-instance view $W(h,h';0)=0$ and $\alpha(h,h';0)=\pi/2$, so each probe is a perfect witness for the other and $\alpha/\lambda\to\infty$ as $\lambda\to0^+$.

For $c_T=+1$ and an uncorrelated medium, $\Psi_0=\Phi\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$ with $P_{12}\Phi=\Phi$: $W(\cdot,\cdot;0)\equiv1$ on $H_V$ iff $\Phi=\lvert\phi\rangle\otimes\lvert\phi\rangle$ up to a phase; otherwise $\alpha/\lambda\to\infty$ for some pair, so agreement with (5.10) requires probes that are not correlated with each other.

Difference of the two probes' records (Δ_h in general, Δ when independent of h)

open_issues: Discrepancy with the expected result, item 1(b): swap invariance is equivalent to an h-independent Δ_h (12.4), not to Δ = 0; Δ = 0 is the termwise property (12.5), which depends on the split (12.6).

Joint places that differ in both probe places: (12.13) is not a function of single-probe distances, since the squared distance has the cross term 2 Re⟨u_h1 − u_h1′ | u_h2 − u_h2′⟩; this matters for the common-space question and is not analysed here.
Beyond leading order: the companion operator C_Ā, and with it Δ and the partner's record, enters W through commutators with B_h; this is not treated.

Reading of the admissible subspace: the full eigenspace of the swap P₁₂ was taken; if a description restricts it further, the only-if direction of (12.3) needs the test vectors of Step 2(iii) to be admissible.
Sign-changing family c_T = −1: not treated beyond item 1; the start φ⊗φ⊗χ of item 2 is not admissible for c_T = −1.

consistency_checks.check: All K_h equal: in Steps 7 and 8 the M_h are then h-independent, so (12.8) gives W = 1 exactly for all λ; consistently, (12.12) and (12.13) vanish, since u_h = u for all h.

Removing p₂: Step 6 with A = {p}, Ā = {c}, M_h = K_h and ω = χ gives ‖Q_χ(K_h − K_h′)χ‖ = ‖u_h − u_h′‖; this is (5.10), an independent input, so it checks Step 6; (12.12) shows that adding p₂ in the state φ changes nothing at leading order.

Swap symmetry of the pair geometry: (12.13) is invariant under h₁↔h₂, under h₁′↔h₂′ and under exchange of its two arguments, matching (12.14), which follows from (3.4) independently of the expansion, and the swap invariance (12.4) of C.
